import pandas as pd

# Source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length1_92/training_0.csv"
]

# List to hold dataframes from all sources
dfs = []

# Load each source CSV, ignoring the first index column (index_col=0)
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the same schema as the target ['user_id', 'email', 'geo'],
# we can union (concatenate) them directly.
# In this case, there is only one source table, so just use it directly.
# But code is ready for multiple sources.

# Concatenate all source dataframes
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Normalize 'user_id' column to lowercase to match target examples style (e.g., user_918)
combined_df['user_id'] = combined_df['user_id'].str.lower()

# Normalize 'email' column to lowercase to match target examples style
combined_df['email'] = combined_df['email'].str.lower()

# The 'geo' column appears to be city names in Russian, keep as is.

# Ensure columns are exactly in target schema order
target_columns = ['user_id', 'email', 'geo']
combined_df = combined_df[target_columns]

# Export the combined dataframe to the target CSV path
combined_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_92/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
